name: SES Road Tire

origin.basis: ENVE Composites USA publishes the official store (site footer).

manufacturing.basis: ENVE does not state where the tire is made.

positioning: ENVE's aero-shaped tubeless-ready road tire with an all-weather silica compound and Vectran barrier, from road racing to all-road widths.
hookless_note: ENVE lists it as compatible with hookless and hooked-bead rims; its tables show the 25c only on 19-21 mm internal rims.
compound: Natural and synthetic rubber with activated silica
weight_basis: ENVE tech-spec table; the page's product-details list gives 255-285 g for 25-31c.

wet_notes.summary: ENVE labels the compound for all-weather performance and claims a confident ride regardless of the weather; no independent wet test recorded.

availability.note: Sold by ENVE's US store; ENVE also runs a European storefront that was not read for this tire.

price_observations.conditions: Official store price on 2026-11-01; one tire; shipping and tax at checkout.

caveats: The page lists two weight sets for 25-29c; the tech-spec figures are shown.
Wet performance is a maker claim.

image.shown: 25 mm black SES Road Tire mounted on a wheel, from ENVE's product page.
image.alt: ENVE SES road tire in 25 mm mounted on a carbon wheel, sidewall logo visible

rights.usage_note: The maker's own product photo, shown from the maker's website; no copy is stored or redistributed by this project, and no license is asserted.

owner_evidence.screening_note: Coded on 2026-11-04 from a fixed source set: the written reviews on the Sigma Sports and bike-components product pages, read in full through each page's own review list (the newest 15 per page when more exist), every reader comment on Bicycle Rolling Resistance's test pages for this tire, and owner comments in coded Xiaohongshu threads. Counted only owners who describe their own riding; star-only ratings, reviews without riding detail, mounting-only impressions and repeats were left out. Comments on one construction's test page count for that construction unless the owner names the other.

reports.summary: A second pair after the first never let the owner down.
A smooth ride in 31 mm, and easy to fit.
Impressive over a good few rides, though hard to seat tubeless.
Fast and comfortable, but the front tire gave way on a shallow pothole within a couple of weeks.
Two tires each suffered a fatal puncture within 100 km, so the owner went back to another brand with tubes.
Rolls really well and the tread resists cuts over about 400 km, but the thin sidewalls deform in fast, loaded corners; 8/10.
Punctured on the first ride; the sealant did not hold and the bead unseated.
Great performance through an Ironman bike course in terrible conditions without a puncture.
Noticeably smoother than the tires it replaced, and undamaged after a 500-mile tour on gritty, potholed roads.
Four winter months: very quick, plenty of grip on cold tarmac and not a single puncture.
No stone cuts after 250 km of autumn riding; rolls smoothly, though not quite as smoothly as the GP5000 TL.
Leaked air through the sidewall moulding, and a very small puncture would not seal with sealant.
Great in 31 mm on an ultra-distance race.
